## Getting data from IPUMS MICS {#c01-ipums}

[IPUMS MICS](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/) lets you work with MICS data across countries without downloading every variable from every original survey file. You select the unit of analysis, surveys and variables. IPUMS then supplies the original UNICEF source data together with syntax that harmonises those selections and builds a pooled extract.

For many multi-country analyses, this reduces data preparation. There is one exception: the MICS6 foundational reading assessment. If the research uses reading outcomes, read [A critical problem with the IPUMS foundational reading data](#ipums-reading-warning) before deciding which variables to extract.

### What IPUMS MICS does

MICS questionnaires and variable coding can differ across countries and survey rounds. IPUMS MICS creates harmonised variables that make comparable concepts easier to identify and analyse.

The IPUMS system also provides variable-level documentation, including:

- variable definitions;
- codes and labels;
- the surveys in which a variable is available;
- the universe — the population for whom a question was asked or a variable is defined;
- questionnaire text; and
- links to survey-specific source documentation.

This documentation is one of the main advantages of IPUMS. IPUMS warns that researchers can make incorrect comparisons if they fail to account for differences in variable universes across MICS surveys. See the [IPUMS MICS FAQ](https://mics.ipums.org/mics-action/faq).

### 1. Register as a MICS user

You must be an approved UNICEF MICS data user to download an IPUMS MICS extract.

IPUMS uses the same UNICEF MICS login credentials. Registration and use are free. See [Getting Started with IPUMS MICS](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/user_guide.shtml).

### 2. Choose your unit of analysis

From GET DATA, IPUMS asks you to choose a unit of analysis. Available units include:

- women;
- children under five;
- children aged 5–17;
- births;
- men;
- household members; and
- household characteristics.

For analyses of the MICS6 Foundational Learning Skills module, the main unit of analysis is usually children aged 5–17.

::: {.alternativebox-header}
**One extract has one unit of analysis**
:::

::: {.alternativebox}
IPUMS MICS allows a single unit of analysis within an extract. If you need information from another unit — household or parent characteristics, for example — some variables may already have been attached or harmonised for your chosen unit, while other analyses may require linking files. IPUMS provides separate [guidance on linking units of analysis](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/linking.shtml).
:::

### 3. Select MICS6 samples

Use the sample-selection interface to choose the MICS6 surveys required for the analysis.

For a multi-country foundational-learning project, keep a record of the exact IPUMS sample identifiers. These identify the specific survey and year more reliably than country names alone.

### 4. Select variables

Browse variables by topic or search for particular concepts and add them to the Data Cart.

Before adding a variable, inspect its documentation. Check:

- whether it is available in all the MICS6 surveys you plan to use;
- whether its meaning is comparable across those samples;
- whether response categories have been harmonised;
- the variable's universe; and
- any survey-specific comparability notes.

Some identifying and technical variables are added to IPUMS extracts automatically. Retain the identifiers and sample variables required to link records and to set up the survey design, even if you do not expect to use them immediately.

### 5. Create the extract

Once you have selected samples and variables, open the Data Cart and choose CREATE DATA EXTRACT.

IPUMS MICS differs from some other IPUMS products in how the final harmonised file is produced. The download contains the source data and Stata syntax. You run the supplied main `.do` file, which applies the IPUMS harmonisation and creates the pooled dataset.

See [IPUMS MICS: General Instructions for Opening an Extract](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/extract_instructions.shtml). Because the extract-building step runs Stata syntax, an R workflow needs Stata once to create the harmonised file; the saved file can then be read and analysed in R.

### A critical problem with the IPUMS foundational reading data {#ipums-reading-warning}

::: {.warningbox-header}
**Do not use the IPUMS MICS reading variables for a MICS6 survey that administered more than one reading passage.**
:::

::: {.warningbox}
In these surveys, IPUMS retains data for only one of the passages. Children assessed using another passage therefore appear to have no data on the harmonised reading variables. This is not ordinary item non-response: it systematically excludes children according to the language or passage in which they were assessed and can make estimates of reading performance seriously misleading.
:::

This issue is especially important in multilingual African countries. MICS6 allowed countries to adapt the reading assessment to local languages. The country-specific source files can therefore contain separate variables for different passages or languages, while the corresponding IPUMS harmonised reading variable represents only one of them.

Malawi MICS 2019–20 administered the reading assessment in English and Chichewa. IPUMS records 1,720 children on `FLWORDSATTEMPT` (the English passage). The original UNICEF data show 3,970 children who attempted the Chichewa passage, of whom 130 also attempted English. An analysis that treated the IPUMS variable as the Malawi reading sample would omit most of the children who actually completed the assessment. The counts and questionnaire details are in [Reading-variable construction](#c07-reading-construction).

The problem is not that IPUMS has miscoded the retained passage; the other passage or passages are absent. This limitation is specific to the harmonised foundational-reading variables in multi-passage surveys. For everything outside the reading assessment, IPUMS harmonisation remains useful.

AFLEARN reconstructs the reading data from the original UNICEF MICS6 country files, retaining all relevant passages and languages. The script [`harmonize-mics-reading-v1.1.R`](https://github.com/datafirst-aflearn/MICS6-Guide/blob/main/Script/harmonize-mics-reading-v1.1.R) constructs research-ready variables from:

- the child's assessment language;
- the correct passage length for that assessment;
- the number of words attempted;
- the number of words read incorrectly or missed;
- the reading comprehension items; and
- the MICS6 reading skip patterns.

The resulting file includes identifiers that allow these variables to be merged onto an IPUMS MICS child extract. You can therefore use IPUMS for harmonised demographic, household, schooling and other background variables, and the AFLEARN reading file for complete foundational reading outcomes. The merge is in [Adding the correct reading data to an IPUMS extract](#c04-ipums-reading).

The reading limitation is a reason to supplement IPUMS, not a reason to avoid it.

[What's in MICS6 data?](#c02-whats-in-data) explains the MICS survey structure and the FLS module. If you already have an IPUMS extract, continue to [Preparing IPUMS data](#c04-prepare-ipums).
